counterevidence_considered.description: The mechanism the issue class is built on is present in the data: 8 planned recorder-nights are excluded, including two nights (N18 and N27) that had detections but fell below the uptime threshold. If any claim were made about the complete planned set, this exclusion would bias it. However, the report makes no complete-domain claim, the planned-unit accounting (40 planned, 32 retained, 8 removed) is fully disclosed, and the stated target matches the task's stated target.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 8 removed nights disclosed; 2 removed nights had detections

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue is present. (1) I searched the report for any sentence attributing the 37.50% rate, or any other quantity, to the complete planned set of 40 recorder-nights; there is none — the only complete-set mention is the accounting line 'Planned recorder-nights: 40' and the parenthetical noting the 8 removed nights are excluded, both of which correctly distinguish planned from retained. (2) I recomputed the screen and rate from the raw CSV (32 retained at >= 8.0 h uptime, 12 detection-positive among them, 12/32 = 37.50%), confirming the arithmetic matches the retained-subset claim rather than silently using a different base. (3) I considered whether the task's retained-subset framing could itself be a mismatch with a larger governing requirement, but the only governing task visible for this case explicitly names the retained subset as the target, and the report's scope note aligns with it. I could not falsify the no-issue verdict.
